sections.body: Storm Atlas is a research-only historical genesis/outcome engine for the North Atlantic and East Pacific. Give it an observed genesis point

Condition on a point. An observed genesis position, or a declared pre-genesis reference cell, with a stated radius and month window. The season floor is a declared boundary, not a preference: an observing-bias gap before 1971 is why the floor sits at 1971, and a cohort reaching behind it is warned rather than pooled silently. Rates are genesis-conditioned and assume formation — not P(forms), not a live feed, not a forecast cone. Retrieve the analog tracks. Every storm in the cohort, with representative members printed under a stated rule — name, season, genesis date, distance from the cell, lifetime peak, and its own landfalls as recorded. Storm Atlas implements no similarity metric, so nothing is ranked as a closest or best analog. Compare contract-row frequencies. Reached TD, TS and Cat 1 through Cat 5, each as exact n/N with its 95% Wilson interval. Time-to-threshold medians with p25 and p75 sit alongside and carry their own n: the min-sample gate governs rates, not medians, so a median can be printed on an n of one or two. Read the n before

An interpolated fix is never allowed to establish a threshold crossing, so time-to-hurricane is never dated off a wind nobody measured. A segment crossing publishes no Saffir-Simpson class where the two bracketing fixes disagree on it — the interpolated wind stays on the row, labelled by detection method; the class derived from it does not. A cohort's defining variable is not reported back as a scored outcome, with one exception left in the open: every cohort returns reached TD at 100%, because a cohort is storms that formed. That row is definitional and carries no information; the panels here start at reached TS. Below min sample a rate
